episodes.199891: A shortwave trough approached the coast Wednesday afternoon. At the surface a stalling cold front intersected the sea breeze boundary while a moderately unstable airmass and steep lapse rates aloft combined to produce thunderstorms with large hail.
episodes.199892: A shortwave trough approached the coast Wednesday afternoon. At the surface a stalling cold front intersected the sea breeze boundary while a moderately unstable airmass and steep lapse rates aloft combined to produce thunderstorms with large hail.
episodes.199903: Abundant moisture and plenty of instability helped to set the stage for a summer-like afternoon across Middle Tennessee on April 23, 2025. Scattered thunderstorms developed across the area during the afternoon and evening hours. With little forcing and wind shear, these thunderstorms were generally non-severe. However, slow storm motions meant that these nearly stationary thunderstorms were able to produce flash flooding in a few areas.
episodes.199944: A line of storms associated with a mid level short wave traversed across portions of the Coastal Bend Wednesday morning of 4/23. These storms produced severe hail across area of San Patricio County.
episodes.200115: A cold front stalling near the area and interacting with a sea breeze circulation within a modestly unstable environment displaying cold temperatures aloft, led to severe thunderstorms capable of producing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.200116: A cold front stalling near the area and interacting with a sea breeze circulation within a modestly unstable environment displaying cold temperatures aloft, led to severe thunderstorms capable of producing large hail.
episodes.200257: A large trough was present over the Central United States, with Central Alabama in a period of west-southwest flow. A shortwave crossing into Alabama from Mississippi sparked the development of a few shower and storms. One storm briefly became severe in Jefferson County and dropped up to quarter-size hail in the Morris area.
episodes.200350: In the early morning hours of the 23rd, convection moved through northwestern Kansas. As one storm moved over southern Graham county, nickel sized hail was reported.
episodes.200387: In the afternoon of the 23rd, a line of storms formed across western Kansas and slowly moved north-northeast. The more intense storms produced hail up to golf ball size.  The strongest wind gust was estimated to be 70 MPH south-southeast of Monument.  A gust of around 45-50 MPH damaged a greenhouse near Hoxie.
episodes.200438: Despite the absence of large scale lift over West Texas, numerous severe thunderstorms were able to form on the afternoon of the 22nd. Strong surface heating existed along and east of a diffuse dryline roughly around the US Highway 385 corridor. Low level moisture return east of the dryline combined with steep mid level lapse rates to create an unstable atmosphere by mid-afternoon. Veering and increasing winds with height allowed some storms to become organized and produced large hail and damaging wind gusts. The initial activity developed over the south-central Texas Panhandle, with additional development farther southwestward into the western South Plains. Large hail up to tennis ball size and gusty outflow winds were common with the strongest storms. One particularly intense storm approached the Matador area (Motley County). This storm was rotating rapidly aloft but never produced a tornado.
episodes.200551: Severe thunderstorms develop over the Palmer Divide and tracked eastward across Lincoln. Hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter fell and winds reached up to 66 mph.
episodes.200686: A shortwave trough moved through Kansas and a dryline/boundary set up across central Kansas. Despite only modest instability and deep shear, a cluster of severe storms developed producing severe hail.
episodes.200694: A compact upper-level shortwave moved across western Kansas on 4/23. An associated boundary stalled in far eastern Colorado with CAPE values of 1500-2000 J/kg. The event started with weaker supercells that eventually transitioned to a messier and incoherent storm mode. The storms produced multiple severe wind and hail reports.
episodes.200705: Scattered severe storms developed in central Kansas and moved into portions of north central Kansas during the late evening hours. While most storms overnight were not severe, a few produced hail to ping pong ball size in Ottawa county.
episodes.200707: Clusters of severe storms develop over portions of northeast Kansas, moving into east central Kansas from mid afternoon to early evening. Large hail to 2 inches in diameter and wind gusts to 60 mph were reported.
episodes.200722: A broad trough across the western United States and a dryline across the Permian Basin and Stockton Plateau resulted in afternoon thunderstorms. Several severe right-moving supercells occurred over the Stockton Plateau, with left-moving supercells moving across western portions of the Permian Basin. In addition, a localized dry microburst resulted in intense wind gusts of 100 MPH or greater near Midland International Air & Space Port.
episodes.200723: There was continued broad troughing across the western United States with a dryline across portions of the Permian Basin south across the Davis Mountains. Splitting supercells occurred with severe weather and blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow across portions of Southeast New Mexico and the Stockton Plateau.
episodes.200724: There was continued broad troughing across the western United States with a dryline across portions of the Permian Basin south across the Davis Mountains. Splitting supercells occurred with severe weather and blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow across portions of Southeast New Mexico and the Stockton Plateau.
episodes.201042: A trough of low pressure linked up with the sea breeze front to produce an isolated severe thunderstorm in the evening. Hail up to golf ball size was reported at and around Albert J Ellis Airport in Richlands.
episodes.201130: Storms erupted along a stationary front during the early evening hours of April 22nd from south central Kansas into western Oklahoma. With plenty of instability and shear, storms quickly became severe as they tracked off to the northeast. We received numerous reports of golf ball sized hail with hail up to tennis ball size reported in Reno County.
episodes.201131: Through the afternoon and evening, scattered thunderstorms developed in southeast NE and southwest IA. The thunderstorms were pulse-like, quickly increasing in strength before weakening just as quick. Overall, hail reports ranged anywhere from 0.50-1 with wind gusts measuring up to 59 mph.
episodes.201355: A weak upper level trough and a slow moving surface front helped spark some scattered severe convection across the CSRA. Moderate wind shear and substantial instability helped organize clusters of storms to produce damaging gusts across Burke County with multiple trees down.
episodes.201425: Weak atmospheric lifting, including some orographic influences, helped spawn a severe thunderstorm in McMinn County that produced severe straight line winds and some damage.
episodes.201429: A nearly stationary boundary across Iowa brought a second day of storms to the area on April 23rd. Warm, moist air streamed into the area through the day, pushing the boundary to the north. While weak shear limited more robust storm development, the moist environment resulted in MLCAPE around 1000-2000 J/kg. Storms developed along the boundary through the evening, producing penny to ping pong ball sized hail, often in large quantities that covered the ground.
episodes.201439: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms produced a few severe hail reports.
episodes.201449: A small cluster of thunderstorms developed in deep southerly flow and a warm, moist airmass behind a warm front. There were steep mid-level lapse rates in this airmass, and these storms produced large hail.
episodes.201680: Loosely organized convection across the Southern High Plains produced a severe-caliber wind gust across western-north Texas during the late evening of the 22nd.
episodes.201708: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of April 22nd east of the dryline. The combination of instability, abundant low level moisture and wind shear allowed storms to become severe and produce hail up to ping pong ball size in the southeast Texas Panhandle. A similar setup occurred on April 23rd where the dryline was situated a little further west which allowed for storms to develop across more of the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. Gusty winds and hail up to tennis ball size occurred on the 23rd as storms moved west.
episodes.201779: The combination of abundant low level moisture and strong instability resulted in a few severe thunderstorms. The severe storms produced large hail and high winds.
episodes.201783: Thunderstorm complexes which developed across the Hill Country and Northwest Texas during the afternoons of April 23 and 24 propagated southeast across North and Central Texas each night into the following mornings. Several instances of large hail and damaging winds occurred with these storms, along with localized flash flooding.
episodes.201815: A weak boundary was draped across central Iowa. Weak forcing prevented storm development for most of the evening, however with increasing theta-e advection in the evening along with an increasing low level jet, a few isolated storms managed to develop along the Highway 30 corridor late. Steep lapse rates created an environment ripe for hail growth with reports ranging from quarter to ping pong ball sized.
episodes.201877: A cold front moved into the region and stalled late in April producing a few days of rain. Flooding occurred at multiple locations and severe storms also developed as a result.
episodes.201954: A storm developed and intensified over south central Kansas during the morning hours of the 23rd. This storm produced two quarter sized hail reports in Rice and McPherson counties.
episodes.202208: A warm front lifted north across Lower East Texas to along the Arkansas/Louisiana border during the afternoon of April 22nd, allowing for the return of warmer, more humid air back north across portions of East Texas and much of North Louisiana. This resulted in ample instability during the afternoon, as an upper level disturbance embedded in the developing southwest flow aloft from the Texas Hill Country into the Lower Mississippi Valley progressed northeast across the area. Sufficient wind shear was also available, and combined with the strong instability, resulted in the development of scattered supercell thunderstorms across portions of Northcentral Louisiana. These storms produced large hail across portions of Natchitoches, Grant, and Ouachita Parishes, before shifting northeast into Northeast Louisiana by early evening.
episodes.202261: A weak shortwave low pushed a warm front through the UP the morning of the 23rd, producing isolated thunderstorms which produced penny sized hail in Baraga County.
episodes.202383: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the South Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon and evening in the vicinity of a cold front. One of the storms produced large hail in Greenwood.
episodes.202685: Several storms produced quarter size hail and heavy rains which resulted in flash flooding across several roads west of Meridian.
episodes.203010: Heavy rainfall occurred across portions of Northern Alabama on April 23rd. A few instances of flash flooding were reported as a result of the heavy rainfall, mainly in Morgan County, AL.
